title: Route a Model per Job
tagline: Each role has one model. Each swap is one line of configuration, and an eval can veto it.

story.problem: One model served every job, so nobody wrote down which model does which job where a reviewer could examine it. When the question came up, one sweep over fifteen labelled vendor replies ranked a cheaper model first. The team switched the classifier to that model. The next run of the same fifteen cases scored 11/15 with six schema failures.
story.solution: A per-role registry lives in agent/lib/models.ts. It has four roles: planner, scout, classifier, and judge. Each role has a default id, an override, a context window, and a written rationale that the app renders. One function resolves every id. assertKnownModel turns the Token Factory price table into an allowlist, so a mistyped id stops the process and cannot benchmark a different model.
story.outcome: The team measured two cheap swaps and refused them. The classifier stayed on Qwen after probe:schema recorded 0/30 structured-output failures against the cheaper candidate's 4/30. The team reverted the scout role after every scout session failed with not one vendor recorded, against a 46/50 baseline. models:compare now runs three rounds and ranks on the worst round.

prerequisites: A Nebius Token Factory API key as NEBIUS_API_KEY in .env.local
npm install at the repo root
A current price snapshot: npm run pricing:refresh
A labelled dataset for at least one role (evals/data/vendor-replies.json)
